title: A Hollow for the Oath
premise: Paloma Hartwell, a mercenary bound by an oath to a god that fell silent a generation ago, has spent his whole life in the valley where magic cannot follow — the only place his sworn blade still counts for anything. When a mute child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Paloma learns the boy's soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain, and that the thirteenth turn of the moon will seal the bargain forever. Leaving the valley means surrendering the god's protection and facing a world where his oath is worthless and his identity as a 'hollow man' — one who traded feeling for survival — marks him as prey. To save the boy, Paloma must steal back the soul from the Undercourt, confront the truth that he himself sold his own heart to survive long ago, and choose between reclaiming what he lost and giving it away; in the end he breaks his oath to the silent god to forge a new one with the found family at his side, trading his stolen years so the child can live whole.
about_author: S. M. Fairweather is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing mercenary company ledgers from the border wars before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people whose bargains have outlived their reasons.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. We meet him mid-contract, escorting a wool merchant through the mist-line where magic dies, and learn the rules of the valley: oaths hold, wonders don't. The emotional beat is quiet loneliness — Paloma is competent, respected, and utterly hollow, going through the motions of a life he cannot feel.

chapters.title: A Knock Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A boy of perhaps eight appears at his door during a storm, unafraid, speaking a language no living scholar knows — yet Paloma understands it, which terrifies him more than the child does. The beat is unease blooming into reluctant tenderness as Paloma takes the boy in for one night.

chapters.title: What the Silence Owes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Maren, the valley's last oath-keeper. She reads the boy's words as a debt notice: his soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain, and the moon's thirteenth turn closes the sale. The beat is dread — Paloma realizes the god he serves went silent because debts like this one came due.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The village votes to give the boy up rather than invite the Undercourt's attention; Paloma, feeling something stir in his hollow chest for the first time in years, refuses and prepares to leave the valley. The beat is defiance — choosing a stranger over safety, and the first crack in his armor of numbness.

chapters.title: The Mist-Line Crossing
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, with the boy (named Wren) beginning to speak simple common tongue. Crossing out of the valley, Paloma's oath-blade goes dead in his hands and the world floods in — color, memory, grief. The beat is disorientation and raw vulnerability: outside the valley, he feels everything he traded away echoing at a distance.

chapters.title: Company of Strays
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, filtered through Paloma's observations. On the road they gather companions: Isbet, a disgraced Undercourt scribe; Torv, a golem abandoned by its maker. Found family forms around campfires. The beat is warmth against danger — Paloma learning that belonging isn't a contract.

chapters.title: The Price Written Twice
chapters.summary: Isbet's POV. In her recovered ledgers she finds two entries for the same date decades ago: Wren's soul sold — and Paloma's heart, sold by Paloma himself to survive a massacre he barely remembers. The beat is betrayal turned inward; Paloma must accept he chose hollowness once, and might choose it again.

chapters.title: Descent Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The party infiltrates the Undercourt during the moon's twelfth turning, navigating a court where every citizen has sold something and bargains are currency. Torv falls holding the gate; Isbet burns her name to buy them passage. The beat is sacrifice compounding — survival always costs someone.

chapters.title: The Court of Sold Things
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Facing the Undercourt's magistrate, Paloma finds his own heart on display among the wares — still beating, still waiting. Offered a choice: take it back and doom Wren, or leave it and stay hollow forever. The climax beat is the ultimate test of identity: he shatters his old oath and offers his reclaimed years instead, buying Wren's soul free.

chapters.title: A New Oath, Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: Shared POV across the surviving family. They return to the valley changed — Paloma mortal-hearted, grieving Torv, but feeling fully for the first time since the massacre. He swears a new oath not to a silent god but to Wren, Isbet, and the life ahead. The resolution beat is quiet hope: the price of survival paid, identity remade by choice.
